notes: Configurations: with_skill = v3 (adds 'a rule that a rewrite hides': when simplifying, state a rule and its reason found in a test, caller or doc beside the new code; and splits the limit line: keep the outside fact, update every statement of what this code does). old_skill = v2 (iteration-2 with_skill runs, reused). without_skill = no skill (iteration-2 runs, reused).

Targeted gain on reason-only-in-test: with_skill 6/6 and 5/6 against old_skill 4/6, 4/6 and without_skill 4/6, 5/6. r1 recorded the warehouse-resend reason beside the new code. r2 recorded 'last update wins' but said it found no reason in the repo, although the test holds it: a genuine fail, no override.

The iteration-2 harm is fixed: on change-contradicts-comment both v3 runs updated every statement of the client's own limit to 250, kept the vendor's free-tier fact of 100, and flagged the conflict in the reply (6/6, 6/6; replies read by hand).
The no-invented-reason gain from v2 held: 5/5 in both with_skill runs; without_skill stays at 4/5.
Non-discriminating: clause-goes-stale and the five easy iteration-1 cases pass in every configuration.

Two with_skill runs (capture-supported-reason r2, comment-only-preserve r2) refused to read SKILL.md because the prompt said 'Do not read anything outside it (apart from the file named above)'. Both were excluded (kept in excluded-runs/) and re-run with wording that says reading the named SKILL.md is required and allowed; both re-runs read it first. All 18 counted with_skill runs read SKILL.md as their first tool call.

Duration outlier: no-invented-reason with_skill r1 took 145 s (43.5k tokens); every other with_skill run took 17-27 s (one reused without_skill run, reason-only-in-test r1, also took 147 s). The time mean and stddev for with_skill are inflated by this one run. Tokens are unchanged across configurations (about 42.6-42.7k).
